concepts: Balanced stance with feet shoulder-width apart

Weight distributed evenly on balls of feet

learning.description: The starting position where both grapplers are standing and facing each other with no grips established. This is where all standing exchanges begin in BJJ.

Keep hands ready for grip fighting
Control distance to prevent immediate attacks
Stay mobile and ready to move in any direction

Keep hands between you and opponent

React to opponent's movement and grip attempts
learning.escape_overview: Not applicable - this is a neutral starting position

concepts: Control opponent's head and posture
Create angle off centerline
Use elbow as frame to create space
Pull down to break opponent's posture
common_mistakes: Standing square instead of creating angle
Gripping without elbow frame on opposite side
Reaching with straight arm instead of bent elbow
key_details: Hand on back of opponent's neck
Elbow bent, pulling down and toward you
Opposite arm frames against opponent's shoulder
Step to side to create angle

learning.description: A standing position where you control the back of your opponent's neck with one hand while framing with the other. Creates posture control and sets up takedowns or guard pulls.
key_concepts: Control opponent's head to control their body
Create angle off the centerline
Use opposite hand as frame to create space
Pull down to break opponent's posture and balance

Place opposite hand on their shoulder or bicep as frame
Step to the side to create angle
Pull neck down while pushing frame to off-balance
maintenance_steps: Keep elbow bent and close to body
Apply constant downward pressure on neck
Frame with opposite arm to prevent them closing distance
learning.escape_overview: Opponent can swim arm inside, establish own collar tie, or create distance by hand fighting
common_mistakes: Pulling straight down without stepping to angle
Standing square in front of opponent
Straight-arming instead of keeping elbow bent

concepts: One arm over opponent's shoulder, one arm under their armpit
Drive forward pressure to off-balance
Keep hips close to control opponent
Use over hook to control posture

Drive forward pressure constantly
Keep hips close to prevent separation
Use overhook to break posture

Wrap overhook over opponent's shoulder

learning.escape_overview: Opponent can pummel for underhooks, create space with frames, or snap you down

concepts: Both arms under opponent's armpits

Control opponent's hips and posture

Elbows tight to sides
Chest drives into opponent

concepts: One arm under opponent's armpit

Opposite hand frames on bicep or shoulder
Head on underhook side

Use opposite arm as frame for distance
Create angle off centerline

concepts: Hands locked around opponent's waist

Control hips for throws and trips

Pull opponent's hips toward you
